assessment.name: Synthetic BOG3-like advisory practice
assessment.context: Fictional small, senior-led growth-systems advisory practice. Values are illustrative and are not claims about BOG3.

summary.interpretation: Maturity and evidence are reported separately. Neither score is a benchmark or causal finding.

dimensions.label: Acquisition / discovery
observations: A clear point of view and website exist, but discovery depends on a narrow set of channels.
risks: Demand may be overly dependent on the principal's existing network.
actions: Map one discovery journey from problem-aware search to a relevant diagnostic entry point.

dimensions.label: Conversion
observations: A contact path exists, but intent and completed inquiry are not reliably distinguished.
risks: CTA activity may be mistaken for a completed lead.
actions: Define and verify one completed-inquiry signal before expanding conversion reporting.

dimensions.label: Lifecycle / follow-up
observations: Follow-up is primarily manual and no shared stage model is visible.
risks: Qualified interest may age without a deliberate next step.
actions: Define a four-stage advisory pipeline and a minimum follow-up expectation for each stage.

dimensions.label: Customer / patient experience
observations: The intended experience is clear, but post-engagement feedback is informal.
risks: Experience quality may depend too heavily on founder memory.
actions: Add a short closeout reflection that captures friction, value, and the next needed outcome.

dimensions.label: Measurement / data quality
observations: Core web measurement exists, but business outcomes are not fully connected to journey signals.
risks: Reporting may optimize engagement rather than qualified progression.
actions: Create a compact measurement map linking discovery, inquiry completion, qualification, and engagement start.

dimensions.label: CRM / MarTech
observations: Several tools support the work, but the relationship record is fragmented.
risks: Manual transfer creates inconsistent context and follow-up.
actions: Choose one system of record and document the minimum fields required for continuity.

dimensions.label: Organizational / process alignment
observations: One senior operator holds most decisions, delivery context, and follow-up.
risks: The operating model has a single-person bottleneck.
actions: Document the recurring review rhythm and the few decisions that require explicit ownership.

priorities.label: Lifecycle / follow-up
priorities.why: Rank reflects 70% maturity gap and 30% evidence uncertainty; it is a triage aid, not proof of business impact.
candidate_actions: Define a four-stage advisory pipeline and a minimum follow-up expectation for each stage.

priorities.why: Rank reflects 70% maturity gap and 30% evidence uncertainty; it is a triage aid, not proof of business impact.
candidate_actions: Choose one system of record and document the minimum fields required for continuity.

priorities.why: Rank reflects 70% maturity gap and 30% evidence uncertainty; it is a triage aid, not proof of business impact.
candidate_actions: Document the recurring review rhythm and the few decisions that require explicit ownership.

system_warnings.interpretation: Initial demand may be created without a reliable follow-up system, creating avoidable leakage.
Tool or channel improvements may not persist until ownership and operating rhythms are clearer.

limitations: Scores reflect assessor judgment against descriptive anchors.
Default weights are equal and have not been empirically calibrated.
Priority ranking estimates gaps and uncertainty, not financial impact or causality.
The diagnostic is a structured hypothesis generator; validate findings with stakeholders and source systems.
